title: Kisa Gotami and the Mustard Seed
text:
Kisa Gotami was a young woman of Savatthi whose only son died when he was just old enough to run about. Unable to accept it, she carried the small body on her hip from house to house, asking everyone for medicine that would cure him. People thought she had lost her mind.

At last a wise man sent her to the Buddha. She begged him for a remedy. He told her he could help, but first she must bring him a few mustard seeds from a house in which no one had ever died.

Mustard seed was common, and she set off with hope. At the first door they gladly offered her some, but when she asked whether anyone had died there, they said, "The living are few, and the dead are many." It was the same at the next house, and the next. In one a father had died, in another a child, in another a wife.

By evening she understood. Death had come to every family in the city. She took her son to the cremation ground and laid him down. Then she returned to the Buddha, became a nun, and later was honored as one of his wise disciples.
lesson: Grief isolates us, as if loss had singled us out. Hearing how others have lost and survived can begin to bring us back to the living.
source: Dhammapada Commentary (Dhammapada-atthakatha) on verse 114; Therigatha Commentary
caveat: The story comes from commentaries written down many centuries after the Buddha's time.
